default.condition: Fail if an in-force claim reads on elements 1–3, has seven or more years of estimated term left in the US, and there is no evidence of a licensing path.

venture_specific.condition: Fail if an in-force US claim covers a synthetic intra-articular ligament for ACL reconstruction with no limitation on material or structure, held by a company that sells a competing synthetic ligament, with estimated expiry past 2033.

evidence.default: No opened claim reads on elements 1–3 alone; every claim that could read requires an unstated material, structure, or degradation profile. The only family with 7+ years (US 11,357,613 and siblings, 'into 2040') requires a two-layer spacer textile with an internal matrix.
evidence.venture_specific: No genus claim found in force: LARS US 7,494,506 'Expired – Lifetime, expires 2026-02-20'; US 6,599,319 'Expired – Lifetime'; broad pre-2000 families not opened.

case_blocked: Biorez's composite-scaffold family (8 US + 16 ex-US by the owner's 2021 count, protection stated 'into 2040') now belongs to CONMED, which sells BioBrace into this surgery; only one member was opened, from a summary page, and CONMED has said nothing about licensing. Biorez's braided-scaffold family ('143, '437) reads on a resorbable braided ligament with distinct sections, and '437 claim 14 drops the non-degrading fiber; it runs to 2030. Zimmer Biomet holds two families whose claims could not be fully read, one active to about 2034 and described for use without a joint replacement. Georgia Tech's US 9,180,000 could not be opened. Applications filed since mid-2025 are unpublished.
verdict_reason: The genus is free — no in-force claim found covering a synthetic ACL ligament fixed to bone as such; both fail conditions cleared on the pages opened. Every live claim that could read turns on unstated elements 4 (material), 5 (structure), and 8 (permanent vs resorbable), and two strategic-held families could not be read. On the pages opened, a permanent single-polymer braided or woven cord with conventional fixation is absent at least one element of every in-force independent claim read; a resorbable sectioned scaffold or a spacer-textile composite moves into the Biorez/CONMED families.

routed_question.question: Settle elements 4 (material class), 5 (structure), 8 (permanent vs resorbable) and 7 (replacement vs augmentation); re-run.

counsel_kit.ask_for: One hour of claim reading against the element list, and a view on whether a formal FTO opinion is warranted — not the opinion. Stage: pre-company, pre-funding, screening.
possible_novelty: Nothing recordable until elements 4–8 are specified
pointers: Do not disclose publicly before counsel has advised on filing.
Status and expiry on a patent page are estimates; counsel verifies on the register.
An application is not a patent, but it can become one; Biorez has said more are pending.
'Patent pending' on a competitor's product means an application exists; find it.
Family members in each jurisdiction can carry different claims.
Keep the element list current; a resorbable scaffold or spacer textile re-runs every map.
A crowded field is a risk; one in-force claim on an essential element with no way around or through it is a wall.

BEAR and BioBrace represent a shift toward repair and augmentation rather than replacement
